stem:
Feroz studies the diagram of figures $F$ and $G$. Figure $G$ is the same shape and size as figure $F$, and $G$ is shown after a flip.

Which claim correctly decides whether $F$ and $G$ are congruent?

options.text: $F$ and $G$ are congruent: same shape and size under exact superimposition, and flipping is allowed.
$F$ and $G$ are congruent because they are both called figures on the page.
Exact fit under superimposition is needed only after congruence is already known.
Congruence here requires a right angle, hypotenuse, and one matching side before the flip can be used.

teacher.key_rationale: Congruent figures match in shape and size under superimposition; rotation or flipping is allowed. Calling them figures, reversing the test order, or importing RHS criteria all miss that hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as congruent L-shapes F and G with G shown as a horizontal flip of F.
